paper_metadata.title: Insights into multi-effects of single element Mo in Ti-rich Ti40Nb30V25−xZr5Mox refractory complex concentrated alloys: Strength-ductility synergy and high-temperature strengthening

evidence.quote: Ti40 Nb30 V25−x Zr5 Mox ( x = 0, 3, and 5, and referred to as Mo0, Mo3, and Mo5) with low densities around 6.2–6.4 g cm−3 were designed.
The Ti40 Nb30 V25−x Zr5 Mox ( x = 0, 3, and 5 in atomic ratio) alloys were prepared by vacuum arc melting under a Ti-gettered argon-protective atmosphere.
the base alloy (Ti40 Nb30 V25 Zr5 ) was regulated to be Ti40 Nb30 V22 Zr5 Mo3 ( ∼6.35 g cm−3 ) and Ti40 Nb30 V20 Zr5 Mo5 ( ∼6.43 g cm−3 ), which are denoted as Mo0, Mo3, and Mo5, respectively.
the base alloy (Ti40 Nb30 V25 Zr5 ) was regulated to be Ti40 Nb30 V22 Zr5 Mo3 ( ∼6.35 g cm−3 ) and Ti40 Nb30 V20 Zr5 Mo5 ( ∼6.43 g cm−3 ), which are denoted as Mo0, Mo3, and Mo5, respectively.
Each ingot ( ∼70 g) was remelted and ﬂipped 12 times in a water-cooled copper hearth.
As-cast ingots were cold-rolled to a 70 % reduction in thickness, followed by a recrystallization annealing at 1223 K for 30 min and water quenching.
